# 08 Fact check: dated facts in the market example

Checked on **2026-09-23** against public sources, by a fact-checking agent. The input was
`notes/facts-to-check.md`, read in full. The model was built from recollection only; this pass
checks those recollections.

**Scope**

- **Values at the cutoff:** all 9 numeric values. The four `judgment.*` and `regime.*` entries
  are authored opinions and were skipped.
- **Dated samples:** all 56 numeric samples. The three `h.pol.*` samples of
  `regime.us_crypto_policy` are authored categories and were skipped.
- **Dated events:** all 32 events: whether each happened, its date, and every figure in its text.

**Time conversion:** calendar time = 2026-01-01 + t x 30.44 days. Event intervals were converted
the same way. The tolerance for an event date was "within a few days". Because a 30.44-day month
drifts, several intervals sit 0.5 to 2 days away from the true date, and none by more than 3 days.

**Result:** cutoff values 9 ok. Dated samples 55 ok and 1 outside interval. Events 32 ok. No item
was "wrong" or "unverifiable".

## Method and sources

Raw data was downloaded wherever an open API existed, so most numbers below are read directly
from the data rather than from summaries.

| process | source used | note |
|---|---|---|
| Fed total assets, reserves | Federal Reserve H.4.1 data package, https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/Output.aspx?rel=H41&filetype=zip. Total assets come from series `RESPPA_N.WW`, the Wednesday level that FRED republishes as WALCL. Reserve balances come from `RESH4R_N.WW`. | |

**Limits:**

- FRED timed out from this environment, so each series was taken from the publication FRED
  copies it from.
- MarketWatch, WSJ and Stooq serve bot checks. These were not bypassed.
- Yahoo's JSON API was rate-limited, so its public history pages were read instead.
- Nothing was signed into, accepted or submitted.

## Findings

### Items that are not ok

1. **hist.sample.h.btc.m49_7: outside the interval.** The miss is small and depends on how the
   sample is defined.
   - **Recorded:** 67,500 [66,000-69,000], for the "BTC/USD daily close near 2021-11-10
     (all-time high then)".
   - **Found:** the 2021-11-10 close was 64,756 (Coin Metrics) or 64,912 (Coinbase). That is
     about 1,100 below the lower bound, after an intraday high of $69,000 that day.
   - **Why 67,500 was recorded:** it is the record daily close of 2021-11-08 (67,542). It is also
     close to the 2021-11-09 close (67,096), the last close in force at the sample's timestamp of
     03:10 UTC on Nov 10.
   - **Suggested fix:** either keep the date and record about 64,800 [63,500-66,500], or re-date
     the sample to 2021-11-08 (t ≈ -49.77) and label it as the cycle's record daily close.
   - **Source:**
     https://community-api.coinmetrics.io/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics?assets=btc&metrics=PriceUSD&frequency=1d&start_time=2021-11-08&end_time=2021-11-10

### Ok, but worth stating in the published note

- **h.sc.m72 (2020-01-01) depends on the aggregator.** DefiLlama's USD-pegged total is 4.17bn,
  below the interval, because it counts USDT at 3.20bn. CoinMarketCap's snapshot gives 4.13bn,
  and DefiLlama appears to leave out USDT on the Omni layer. Coin Metrics and CoinMarketCap give
  about 5.2-5.9bn, which is inside the interval. If the published model names DefiLlama as its
  frame, the lower bound of 4.5 fails on that aggregator's own figure.
- **Some point values are notably off but still inside wide intervals:**
  - `h.tga.m31`: 40 recorded vs 23.4 found.
  - `h.sc.m24`: 135 recorded vs 129.8 found.
  - `fed.total_assets_usd_tn` at the cutoff: 6.55 recorded vs 6.641 found, for the nearest
    weekly level (a year-end bulge).
  - `h.tga.m2`: 950 recorded vs 926.3 found.
  - `stablecoins.usd_supply_usd_bn`: 270 recorded vs 277-281 found.
- **The Q4 2025 drawdown figure depends on the measure.** "About 30-35%" holds, but the fall
  from the intraday high was 36% to the intraday trough and 31% to the year-end close.
- **Event intervals drift with the 30.44-day month.** The whitepaper and genesis intervals end
  10-14 hours before the actual events. The Strategic Bitcoin Reserve order, GENIUS signing,
  Terra, Celsius and SVB intervals begin 0.5-3 days after the first actual date. All are within
  the few-days tolerance.
- **The reserve-management purchases event can be upgraded from "moderate confidence".** It is
  confirmed by the FOMC statement and by NY Fed operation results starting 2025-12-12.
- **The definitions used here should be stated alongside the model.**
  - BTC closes are Coin Metrics reference-rate closes at 00:00 UTC.
  - DXY is the Yahoo DX-Y.NYB close.
  - ETF flows are Farside daily totals as published on 2026-09-23. Farside revises late prints.
  - The fiat-backed stablecoin total uses DefiLlama's `pegMechanism` classification. It changes
    by about 4bn depending on whether tokenized funds are counted.

It is ordinal, so +2 is not twice +1. (2) regime.btc_monetary_coupling: which relation dominated BTC's response to dollar conditions. (3) regime.crypto_leverage: the derivatives leverage state. (4) regime.us_crypto_policy: supplied by the modeler with its rubric. nodes.text: {"aspect":"broaderContext","focalInterval":{"start":-24,"end":0},"status":"represented","assessment":"The focal crypto processes sit inside dollar conditions set by the Fed and the Treasury. Across the focal window, the rate path (5.50% to 3.75% upper bound), runoff (slowed in June 2024 and April 2025, ended December 2025) and plumbing shifts (the TGA drawdown in H1 2025, then its rebuild after July 2025 once ON RRP was exhausted) moved in different directions at different times. The account therefore keeps them as separate processes instead of one liquidity index. The dollar's H1 2025 decline and the stablecoin reserves invested in bills connect the sector both ways. Relevant but not modeled as processes: Bank of Japan policy (recorded as the August 2024 unwind event), global M2, equity valuations and AI-sector risk appetite, fiscal deficits. Each is excluded for scope and recorded as an event or note.","processIds":["us.fed_funds_upper_pct","fed.total_assets_usd_tn","us.on_rrp_usd_bn","us.tga_usd_bn","usd.dxy_index","us.real_yield_10y_pct","stablecoins.tbill_reserves_usd_bn"],"eventIds":["ev.fed_cuts_2024","ev.fed_cuts_2025","ev.qt_taper_2024","ev.qt_taper_2025","ev.debt_limit_2025_tga_drawdown","ev.obbba_tga_rebuild_2025","ev.repo_pressure_qt_end_2025","ev.yen_carry_unwind_2024","ev.tariff_shock_2025"],"sourceIds":["src.fomc.2024_2025","src.fed_balance_sheet","src.rrp_tga","src.dollar_yields","src.leverage_events","src.macro_events_2025"],"boundary":"The US dollar monetary system: FOMC policy rate and guidance, the Fed balance sheet and bank reserves, Treasury cash management (TGA) and the ON RRP facility, the dollar's exchange value and real yields. nodes.text: {"aspect":"conceptVariation","focalInterval":{"start":-24,"end":0},"status":"represented","assessment":"Bitcoin's monetary meaning is framed differently across dates and actors: peer-to-peer cash against bailouts (2008-09), debasement hedge (macro investors, 2020), liquidity-sensitive risk asset (2022 behaviour and commentary), and institutional allocation and strategic reserve (2024-25). These are attributed framings with dated contexts; the model does not assert that BTC's nature changed. It separates world changes, such as the ETF conduit existing from 2024-01-11 and the stablecoin statute from 2025-07-18, from framing differences the evidence does not settle ('digital gold' versus 'risk asset'). 'Dollar liquidity' also varies between communities: central bankers mean reserve and funding conditions, crypto commentators often mean a net-liquidity heuristic or global M2. The model keeps the components and does not adopt either community's index.","processIds":[],"eventIds":["ev.bitcoin_whitepaper","ev.genesis_block","ev.fed_zlb_qe_2020","ev.fed_first_hike_2022","ev.spot_btc_etf_launch","ev.strategic_btc_reserve_eo"],"sourceIds":["src.btc_meaning_framings","src.bitcoin_origin","src.etfs","src.regulation_policy"],"conceptIds":["concept.btc_monetary_meaning","concept.btc_as_p2p_cash_alternative","concept.btc_as_debasement_hedge","concept.btc_as_liquidity_risk_asset","concept.btc_as_institutional_allocation","concept.dollar_liquidity"],"abstractCutIds":["acut.btc_meaning.framings"]}

nodes.text: {"aspect":"longerTerm","focalInterval":{"start":-24,"end":0},"status":"represented","assessment":"The longer horizon starts with the 2008 crisis because Bitcoin's founding framing formed against bank bailouts and the first QE. That origin is the source of the later 'debasement hedge' reading, which the focal evidence does not support as the dominant behaviour. The 2020-2022 zero-rate and QE surge coincided with a stablecoin expansion from about $5B to about $180B and BTC's rise to about $69K, carried by stablecoin and leverage conduits. The 2022-2023 tightening coincided with the collapse of crypto credit (Terra, Celsius, FTX) and a stablecoin contraction. The 2023 TGA rebuild drained ON RRP rather than reserves. The focal era differs structurally: a regulated ETF conduit exists from 2024-01-11 and corporate treasuries grow, so the channel mix, not only the monetary stance, changed. The long events are episodes, not numerical trends; dated values are sampled separately. No data are represented for 2014-2019 (unknown at this resolution).","processIds":["us.fed_funds_upper_pct","fed.total_assets_usd_tn","stablecoins.usd_supply_usd_bn","btc.price_usd","regime.crypto_leverage"],"eventIds":["ev.era.qe_origin_2008_2014","ev.era.pandemic_easing_2020_2022","ev.era.tightening_2022_2023","ev.fed_zlb_qe_2020","ev.terra_collapse","ev.ftx_collapse","ev.svb_usdc_depeg_2023","ev.debt_limit_2023_tga_rebuild"],"sourceIds":["src.bitcoin_origin","src.fomc.2020_2023","src.fed_balance_sheet","src.stablecoins","src.crypto_credit_2022","src.rrp_tga"],"interval":{"start":-208,"end":0}}

Confidence high. 2020-03-03 emergency cut of 50bp; 2020-03-15 cut to 0-0.25% and restart of large-scale purchases; 2020-03-23 purchases made open-ended. Purchases tapered from November 2021 and ended in March 2022. 2022-03-16 first hike (+25bp to 0.25-0.50%). Four consecutive 75bp hikes in June, July, September and November 2022. Final hike 2023-07-26 to 5.25-5.50%, held there until September 2024.

src.modeler.hypotheses: Modeler's authored channel hypotheses (this run)
nodes.text: Authored hypotheses by the modeler, not findings. H1 stablecoin conduit: growth in USD stablecoin supply adds on-chain dollar settlement liquidity, but supply also responds to issuer economics (reserve yield rises with the policy rate) and to offshore demand for dollars. H2 ETF conduit: since 2024-01-11 spot ETP creations carry TradFi allocators' decisions, sensitive to rate expectations, equity risk appetite and basis-trade economics, into spot demand. H3 leverage amplifier: derivatives leverage, whose funding cost and margin depend on dollar rates and risk appetite, amplifies moves through liquidations. H4 valuation channel: repricing through the real discount rate and risk premium without a specific flow conduit. H5 plumbing: the 'net liquidity' heuristic (Fed assets minus TGA minus ON RRP) is widely used by market commentators but contested; the model keeps its components as separate processes and does not assert the heuristic. H6 corporate-treasury conduit: equity- and convertible-funded corporate buying. These channels overlap and compete; the model does not assign causal laws.

src.rrp_tga: NY Fed ON RRP results and Daily Treasury Statement, TGA (recalled)
nodes.text: Recalled by the modeler (Claude Opus 5.5) from training data; not retrieved or checked against the primary source in this run. Levels approximate; confidence moderate. ON RRP usage peaked around $2.5T near end-2022. It fell through 2023-2024 as money funds moved into new Treasury bills after the debt limit was suspended by the Fiscal Responsibility Act (2023-06-03). Usage was roughly $0.1-0.5T during 2024 and near zero (tens of billions) by autumn 2025. TGA: rebuilt to about $0.7-0.8T in H2 2023. The debt limit was reinstated 2025-01-02 and the TGA was drawn down under extraordinary measures in H1 2025. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed 2025-07-04) raised the limit by $5T, and the TGA was rebuilt toward Treasury's roughly $850B cash target by October 2025. Because ON RRP was nearly exhausted, this rebuild drew down bank reserves more directly than the 2023 rebuild did. Repo rates rose above the Fed's administered rates, and Standing Repo Facility use set records in late October 2025.

src.stablecoin_policy: SVB/USDC depeg 2023 and GENIUS Act 2025 (recalled)
nodes.text: Recalled by the modeler (Claude Opus 5.5) from training data; not retrieved or checked against the primary source in this run. Confidence high. Silicon Valley Bank failed 2023-03-10. Circle disclosed about $3.3B of USDC reserves held there; USDC traded below $0.90 on 2023-03-11 and re-pegged after the 2023-03-12 federal backstop (depositors protected; Bank Term Funding Program). The GENIUS Act, signed 2025-07-18, creates a federal framework for payment stablecoins with 1:1 reserves in cash, short Treasury bills and similar assets.

nodes.text: Recalled by the modeler (Claude Opus 5.5) from training data; not retrieved or checked against the primary source in this run. About $5-6B at the start of 2020; peak about $180-190B in April 2022, including about $18B of algorithmic UST; UST collapsed in May 2022; low about $120-125B around October 2023; about $130-140B in January 2024; about $200B at end-2024; about $250B in mid-2025; about $300B by October 2025. USDT is the largest (roughly 60% share), USDC second. Issuer reserves are held mainly in short Treasury bills, reverse repo and cash. Tether reported more than $100B of US Treasury exposure in 2025 attestations.

nodes.text: Competing explanations kept open. (a) Price-of-money reading: BTC responds to the expected policy path and real yields. (b) Quantity reading: BTC responds to reserves and plumbing (the contested 'net liquidity' heuristic). (c) Flow-conduit reading: since 2024 identifiable flows (ETF creations, corporate treasuries) dominate, and monetary conditions matter only through those allocators. (d) Crypto-native reading: halvings, leverage cycles and regulatory shifts dominate. For the late-2024 rally, the election (regulatory expectations) and the rate cuts coincide, so the evidence here cannot separate them.

nodes.text: Feedback from the crypto sector into the enclosing system: fiat-backed stablecoin issuers invest reserves mainly in short Treasury bills, and the GENIUS Act writes that reserve composition into law. Stablecoin growth therefore adds structural demand for bills, a channel from crypto into Treasury funding. The size of this feedback (stablecoins.tbill_reserves_usd_bn) is left unknown because the modeler cannot reconstruct the aggregate.

nodes.text: Q4 2025 anomaly: the policy rate was cut twice more and runoff ended, yet BTC fell from about $126K to about $80-90K. Candidate explanations, unresolved: the October leverage flush; ETF outflows as TradFi de-risking; reserve scarcity from the TGA rebuild and repo pressure, which the rate cuts did not offset until runoff ended; compression of treasury-company premia; and holder distribution tied to a four-year-cycle narrative. The anomaly shows that transmission is not a fixed sign from easing to price.

nodes.text: Recalled by the modeler (Claude Opus 5.5) from training data; not retrieved in this run. Supplementary facts used by samples that the original evidence items do not state. FOMC: first post-crisis hike 2015-12-16 to 0.25-0.50%; hikes through 2018-12-19 to 2.25-2.50%; cuts on 2019-07-31, 2019-09-18 and 2019-10-30 to 1.50-1.75%. Fed total assets were about $0.9T before September 2008 and about $4.5T at the end of QE3 (October 2014). The 10-year TIPS yield was about -1% in late 2021. The TGA fell to tens of billions of dollars in early June 2023 near the debt-limit deadline. BTC's close on 2021-11-10 was about $65-68K, with an intraday high near $69K. Confidence: high for the FOMC dates and ranges, moderate for the levels.

nodes.subject: ev.assess.channels.2020_2021
nodes.text: Episode: March 2020 to November 2021. US monetary conditions: emergency cuts to 0-0.25% in March 2020 and open-ended asset purchases; Fed total assets rose from about $4.2T to about $8.7T; the 10-year real yield fell to about -1%; the dollar weakened in 2020. Crypto: BTC rose from a March 2020 low near $5K to an all-time high near $69K on 2021-11-10. USD stablecoin supply grew from about $5B to well over $100B. Derivatives leverage and crypto lending expanded, with record open interest near the top. The first large corporate treasury purchases began in August 2020, and a carmaker bought about $1.5B of BTC in early 2021. No US spot bitcoin ETP existed. A widely read May 2020 hedge-fund letter framed BTC as a debasement hedge. Facts recalled by the modeler from public records (not retrieved); approximate magnitudes.

nodes.text: Episode: March to December 2022. US monetary conditions: hikes from 0.25% to 4.50% at the upper bound, including four 75bp hikes, and balance-sheet runoff from June 2022; the 10-year real yield rose from about -1% to about +1.5%; the dollar index peaked near 114 in September. Crypto: BTC fell from about $40-48K in March to about $15.5K in November. Terra's UST and LUNA collapsed in May; Three Arrows Capital and Celsius failed in June-July; FTX failed in November. USD stablecoin supply fell from about $185B (including UST) to about $140B. No US spot bitcoin ETP existed. US regulators increased enforcement. Facts recalled by the modeler from public records (not retrieved); approximate magnitudes.

nodes.subject: ev.assess.channels.2024
nodes.text: Episode: January to December 2024. US monetary conditions: the policy rate was held at 5.25-5.50% until September, then cut by 100bp to 4.25-4.50% (September-December); runoff was slowed in June; ON RRP balances drained, cushioning bank reserves; the dollar index was roughly 100-108. Crypto: US spot bitcoin ETPs launched on 2024-01-11 and took in about $35B net during the year; the April halving cut new supply; BTC rose from about $42-46K to a March high near $73.7K, fell to about $49-54K during the August carry-trade unwind that followed a Bank of Japan hike, then rose after the November 5 election of a crypto-favourable administration, crossing $100K on December 5 and ending near $93K. USD stablecoin supply rose from about $135B to about $200B. The largest corporate holder more than doubled its holdings during the year, to about 446K BTC. Facts recalled by the modeler from public records (not retrieved); approximate magnitudes.

nodes.text: Episode: January to early October 2025. US monetary conditions: the policy rate was held at 4.25-4.50% until a 25bp cut on September 17; runoff was slowed to $5B of Treasuries a month from April; under the reinstated debt limit the TGA was drawn down in H1 (adding reserves), then rebuilt after the July 4 debt-limit increase once ON RRP was nearly exhausted (draining reserves); the dollar index fell about 10% in H1. Crypto: BTC fell from about $109K in January to about $75K during the April tariff shock, then rose to an all-time high near $126K on October 6. USD stablecoin supply grew from about $200B to about $300B; the GENIUS Act (July 18) created a statutory framework; a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve executive order was issued on March 6. Spot ETP inflows continued (cumulative net from about $35B to about $60B), and listed digital-asset-treasury companies multiplied. Facts recalled by the modeler from public records (not retrieved); approximate magnitudes.

nodes.subject: ev.assess.channels.q4_2025
nodes.text: Episode: October 6 to December 31, 2025. US monetary conditions: the policy rate was cut on October 29 and December 10 (to 3.50-3.75% at the upper bound; the December cut is recalled with moderate confidence); runoff ended on December 1 after repo-market pressure in late October; reserve-management Treasury-bill purchases began in mid-December; a federal shutdown ran from October 1 to November 12. Crypto: after a US threat of 100% tariffs on Chinese goods, the largest recorded liquidation cascade (about $19B) hit on October 10-11; BTC fell from about $126K to about $80-82K by November 21 and traded roughly $85-95K in December; US spot ETPs saw notable net outflows in November; share-price premia of digital-asset-treasury companies compressed. USD stablecoin supply was roughly flat to slightly higher, near $300B. Facts recalled by the modeler from public records (not retrieved); approximate magnitudes.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# 08 Fact check: dated facts in the market example

Checked on **2026-09-23** against public sources, by a fact-checking agent. The input was
`notes/facts-to-check.md`, read in full. The model was built from recollection only; this pass
checks those recollections.

**Scope**

- **Values at the cutoff:** all 9 numeric values. The four `judgment.*` and `regime.*` entries
  are authored opinions and were skipped.
- **Dated samples:** all 56 numeric samples. The three `h.pol.*` samples of
  `regime.us_crypto_policy` are authored categories and were skipped.
- **Dated events:** all 32 events: whether each happened, its date, and every figure in its text.

**Time conversion:** calendar time = 2026-01-01 + t x 30.44 days. Event intervals were converted
the same way. The tolerance for an event date was "within a few days". Because a 30.44-day month
drifts, several intervals sit 0.5 to 2 days away from the true date, and none by more than 3 days.

**Result:** cutoff values 9 ok. Dated samples 55 ok and 1 outside interval. Events 32 ok. No item
was "wrong" or "unverifiable".

## Method and sources

Raw data was downloaded wherever an open API existed, so most numbers below are read directly
from the data rather than from summaries.

| process | source used | note |
|---|---|---|
| Fed total assets, reserves | Federal Reserve H.4.1 data package, https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/Output.aspx?rel=H41&filetype=zip. Total assets come from series `RESPPA_N.WW`, the Wednesday level that FRED republishes as WALCL. Reserve balances come from `RESH4R_N.WW`. | |
| Fed funds target | Fed target-range history, https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm, plus the FOMC statements | The history page lists effective dates, one day after each decision |
| 10-year real yield | U.S. Treasury daily par real yield curve, 10-year | This is the source of H.15 and FRED DFII10 |
| TGA | Daily Treasury Statement, "TGA Closing Balance", via https://api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov | |
| ON RRP, standing repo, bill purchases | New York Fed Markets API, https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/rp/results/search.json and /api/tsy/all/results/summary/search.json | |
| BTC/USD | Coin Metrics community API `PriceUSD`, the reference-rate close at 00:00 UTC that ends each day. Coinbase Exchange daily UTC candles were used as a cross-check. | The two agree within 0.5% on every date checked |
| DXY | Yahoo Finance history for DX-Y.NYB (the ICE US Dollar Index) | Read through a page-fetch tool. The 2025 close was cross-checked against CNBC and NPR year-end reporting (98.28). |
| Stablecoins | DefiLlama stablecoins API: the total for USD-pegged coins, and per-asset charts for the fiat-backed sum, classified by DefiLlama's `pegMechanism` | For 2020, also Coin Metrics `SplyCur` and a CoinMarketCap snapshot |
| US spot BTC ETF flows | Farside Investors all-data table, https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/. Daily totals were summed from 2024-01-11. | As published on 2026-09-23 |
| Bitcoin blocks | mempool.space API | |
| Laws, orders, events | whitehouse.gov, federalreserve.gov, FDIC, Bank of Japan, CRS, CRFB, BIS, and news reporting (CoinDesk, CNBC, NPR, Reuters via US News, Fortune, Washington Post, Bankless, CoinGlass) | |

**Limits:**

- FRED timed out from this environment, so each series was taken from the publication FRED
  copies it from.
- MarketWatch, WSJ and Stooq serve bot checks. These were not bypassed.
- Yahoo's JSON API was rate-limited, so its public history pages were read instead.
- Nothing was signed into, accepted or submitted.

nodes.text: Derived diagnostic comparing Jev's driver Cut (v1) with the modeler's (v2). v2 is projected onto v1 by moving access_adoption_demand into the remainder; TV is the total variation, the minimum share that must move to turn one allocation into the other. 2020_2021: TV 0.28 (v1 remainder 0.15 -> v2 0.10; US-monetary share Jev 0.83 vs modeler 0.55); 2022: TV 0.15 (v1 remainder 0.14 -> v2 0.05; US-monetary share Jev 0.40 vs modeler 0.45); 2024: TV 0.27 (v1 remainder 0.36 -> v2 0.10; US-monetary share Jev 0.02 vs modeler 0.15); 2025_to_october: TV 0.41 (v1 remainder 0.16 -> v2 0.10; US-monetary share Jev 0.17 vs modeler 0.15); q4_2025: TV 0.43 (v1 remainder 0.02 -> v2 0.10; US-monetary share Jev 0.00 vs modeler 0.10). The two estimators disagree most for 2025. Jev gives US crypto policy 0.64 (January-October) and crypto-internal dynamics 0.85 (Q4), while the modeler spreads responsibility across policy, access demand, crypto-internal dynamics and a residual monetary share of 0.10-0.15. They agree that US monetary conditions dominated 2020-21 more than any later episode. They also agree that monetary conditions explain less of BTC's moves in the ETF era than in 2020-22. Both are AI judgments on the same recalled situation texts, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. The divergences are diagnostics, not new semantic numbers.

nodes.text: Revisit of the broader-context and longer-term reviews after the local findings. The context review set the US monetary system as the enclosing system, and the 2020-22 history supports that reading for that period. The focal findings change the account for 2024-25 in three ways. (1) The enclosing system that matters for crypto widened. US crypto policy and new access wrappers, which the original review treated as a gate, carried more explanatory weight than the rate path or reserves in both allocations. (2) The stablecoin conduit grew from about $135B to about $305B while the Fed balance sheet shrank by about $1.1T. Its growth therefore cannot be read as a direct image of dollar liquidity. The functional-role opening (acut.stablecoin.roles) was needed. (3) The feedback into the enclosing system strengthened: bill-backed stablecoins, now under a statute, are a growing buyer of Treasury bills, although their size stays unknown in this model (stablecoins.tbill_reserves_usd_bn). The longer-term reading of BTC as a liquidity-sensitive risk asset (2020-22) did not carry over intact into the ETF era. This is a change in the modeled world's channel structure, not a change in framing. The debasement-hedge framing stays a framing: neither the samples nor the Cuts support it as the dominant behaviour.

nodes.text: Where the modeler disagrees with the Jev allocations (kept as disagreement, not overwritten). (1) corporate_treasury gets about 0 in every episode, although the largest corporate holder bought about 250K BTC in 2024 and digital-asset-treasury companies multiplied in 2025. One reading is that such buying was driven by equity-market access rather than by US monetary conditions, so a monetary-conditional question excludes it. (2) ETF flows get only 0.10 (2024) and 0.04 (2025) of the monetary part; the modeler would weight them higher. (3) The 2024 driver remainder of 0.36 is too large to ignore. It points to a missing driver category, new access and adoption demand (the ETF wrapper and corporate treasuries), which is neither monetary, nor policy, nor crypto-internal. The next model revision adds that category in a second, modeler-authored version of the driver question, keeping this version unchanged.

The retrieved value is filed as a report at the same date and linked to the recalled sample with a corrects edge. The five in-range samples with the largest point differences are also filed as retrieved reports and linked with checks edges: the TGA on 2023-06-02 (40 recalled, 23.4 found) and near 2025-11-01 (950 and 926.3); USD-pegged stablecoins on 2024-01-01 (135, and 129.84 on DefiLlama); fiat-backed stablecoins at the cutoff (270, and 277.3 to 281.4 depending on whether tokenized funds count); and Fed total assets at the cutoff (6.55, and 6.641 for the Wednesday 2025-12-31 level, which includes a year-end bulge; the neighbouring weeks were 6.581 and 6.574). The reserve-management purchases event, recorded at moderate confidence, is confirmed by the 2025-12-10 FOMC statement and the New York Fed's first bill purchase on 2025-12-12. Definitions used by the check: BTC closes are Coin Metrics reference-rate closes at 00:00 UTC; the dollar index is the ICE close as shown by Yahoo (DX-Y.NYB); ETF flows are Farside daily totals as published on 2026-09-23; stablecoin totals follow DefiLlama. DefiLlama's 2020-01-01 total (4.17) omits Tether on Omni and falls below the recalled interval, while Coin Metrics and CoinMarketCap give 5.2 to 5.9, inside it. Event intervals converted at 30.44 days per month sit up to three days from the actual dates. The check changes nothing the modeler recorded: the recalled samples, the world state at the cutoff, and every allocation and judgment stay as they were, beside the retrieved reports.

nodes.text: What this model does not show. It is an illustrative, revisable explanatory account, not a forecast, trading signal or investment analysis. It does not identify causal effects: the Cuts allocate explanatory responsibility from a perspective, and the Jev ones depend on situation texts the modeler wrote. It holds no retrieved data. Every value is recalled or judged, and only the FOMC ranges are exact. Its resolution is monthly and episodic, with no daily flows, funding rates or order books. ON RRP and stablecoin T-bill reserves are unknown at the cutoff. Nothing after 2025-12-31 is represented, although the run date is 2026-09-23. Non-US central banks, global M2, equity and AI-sector risk appetite, altcoins and Ethereum appear only as events or answer categories. There are no transition laws, so the model cannot simulate a policy change. What would improve it: retrieved series for every sampled process, issuer attestations, ETP flow and derivatives data, and later observations against which the channel allocations could be tested.

nodes.text: Provisional reading for the model's question (AI inference on recalled evidence; not a causal identification or forecast). In 2020-2022, changes in US monetary conditions explain most of BTC's large moves and travel mainly through on-chain stablecoin liquidity and crypto leverage and credit. The 2022 unwind is shared with crypto-internal failures. In the spot-ETF era (2024-2025), US monetary conditions explain a small share of BTC's moves in these allocations. Regulatory and political shifts, new access demand and crypto-internal leverage account for more. When monetary conditions did matter in 2025, the allocations route them through stablecoin liquidity more than ETF flows. In Q4 2025, easing coincided with a leverage-driven fall. Stablecoin supply rose almost monotonically from about $135B to about $305B while the Fed balance sheet shrank. So the stablecoin conduit's growth reflects offshore dollar demand, issuer economics and regulation, not only dollar liquidity (see acut.stablecoin.roles). This reading holds only at the model's monthly resolution and depends on the situation texts the modeler wrote.

nodes.text: Review of the ten Jev-estimated channel Cuts (ingest proposal estimate.ffba0703; usage 8,302 input and 715 output tokens). Approved as recorded AI inference, not canon. q.driver, the US-monetary share of each episode's BTC move: 0.83 in 2020-21 (confidence 0.78); 0.40 in 2022 against 0.46 crypto-internal (confidence 0.33); 0.02 in 2024, where us_crypto_policy is 0.34, crypto_internal 0.28 and the remainder 0.36 (confidence 0.19); 0.17 in January-October 2025 against 0.64 crypto policy (confidence 0.56); 0.00 in Q4 2025 against 0.85 crypto-internal (confidence 0.80). q.conduit, the route of that monetary part: stablecoin liquidity 0.85 in 2020-21 and 0.73 in 2025 to October; leverage and credit 0.43 in 2022 (valuation 0.35) and 0.55 in Q4 2025; in 2024 stablecoins 0.42 and ETF flows 0.10. Caveats: q.conduit is conditional on the US-monetary part of q.driver. Where that part is near zero (2024, Q4 2025) its shares carry little information. The question states this conditioning, but the ingest tool gave no way to declare it as a conditioning address on the Cut. Low confidence for 2022 and 2024 means these allocations should not be read as settled.

nodes.text: Review of the historical samples (modeler). Approved as a record of dated samples, not as verification. The policy-rate path is exact. Balance-sheet, TGA, dollar, real-yield, stablecoin, ETF-flow and price values are approximate and carry intervals; replacing them with retrieved series would turn them into observations. What the samples show: from January 2024 to the cutoff, the policy rate fell 1.75 points, Fed assets fell by about $1.1T, USD-pegged stablecoin supply rose from about $135B to about $305B, and US spot ETPs took in about $50-65B net. BTC rose from about $46K to highs near $126K and ended the period near $80-100K. The two conduits grew fastest in 2024 and mid-2025, while the balance sheet was still shrinking. That fits a flow-and-regulation reading at least as well as a reserve-quantity reading, but the samples cannot separate them. ON RRP stays without samples because it has no native record.

nodes.text: Review of the retrospective judgment samples (modeler). Across the long horizon the accommodation rank goes +2 (2020-21), -2 (mid-2022), -1 (2023 to mid-2025) and 0 (November 2025). The Jev estimate at t = 0 is about +1. Over the same dates the coupling reading shifts from liquidity-coupled (2021-22) through crypto-native (2023) to flow-dominated (2024-25). The two series are not independent evidence: both are my judgments, made with hindsight, on the same recalled record. Rubric issue: the +1 anchor text says 'adding reserves (for example bill purchases)', so the Fed's December 2025 reserve-management bill purchases map to +1 even though the Fed framed them as technical, not a change of stance. A revised rubric that separated technical reserve management from stance would move t = 0 toward 0 without any change in the world. That is a rubric effect, not a world change, and it is left visible rather than edited away. Leverage judgments avoid hindsight: 2025-10-01 is judged elevated, not extreme.

nodes.text: Category revision (model revision 3). The Jev driver Cut for 2024 in vocabulary v1 left 0.36 unallocated, the largest remainder in the model. Following the guide, a large remainder signals a missing category. Candidate: new access and adoption demand, the demand the regulated ETP wrapper and corporate-treasury adoption made possible. It is not a monetary condition, not the policy act that permitted it, and not crypto-internal. Revision 3 adds it as the native concept concept.access_adoption_demand and adds a second driver Cut (vocabulary v2) under each assessment event. The estimator budget was spent, so the v2 weights are the modeler's own coarse allocations (0.05 grid), not Jev outputs. The v1 Cuts stay as they were: the new vocabulary is another view of the same episodes, not a correction of Jev's numbers and not a change in the world.

nodes.text: Definition correction (revisions 1 and 1b). While sampling history I found that my recalled stablecoin figures (about $305B at end-2025) are aggregator totals for all USD-pegged stablecoins, but revision 0 filed them under a process defined as fiat-backed only. Revision 1 corrected the definition in place, but the world refused it: a world revision may not change a process's unit, frame or scale. So revision 1 (15ef65cc...) stays registered and unadopted. Revision 1b keeps the original definition, revises its t = 0 estimate to 270 (interval 250-290, fiat-backed only), and adds stablecoins.usd_pegged_supply_usd_bn for the all-USD-pegged total (305) and its history. This is a changed estimate and a new category, not a change in the world. The revision-0 value of 305 remains in the history.

nodes.text: Protocol step 9, causal use and conservation. The model declares no executable laws (executableLawCount 0), so there is no intervention to run: changing one input cannot propagate, and an irrelevant-input stability test is vacuous. That is deliberate. The evidence supports sampled values and attributed allocations, not transition functions. Conservation across revisions: revisions 1b-3 preserved every referent, event, process identity and earlier value. The one changed estimate (fiat-backed stablecoins, 305 to 270) went through an explicit world revision that keeps both heads. The v2 driver vocabulary is a second question, not an opening of the v1 Cut, so no Close or recomposition check applies. The conduit Cuts are conditional on the monetary share in their question text only; no conditioning address is declared.
